newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast prods edge up amid tight supplies.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast prods edge up amid tight supplies.

text.p: U.S. West Coast products prices edged higher in morning trade, as perceptions of tight supplies offset slight declines in futures prices, traders said.
West Coast petroleum products generally rose a half cent amid shutdowns at Mobil, Chevron, and Unocal refineries in California.
This helped curb any decline as January gasoline futures fluctuated around 71 cents a gallon and heating oil fell 0.18 cents a gallon to 74 cents.
In Los Angeles, conventional unleaded gasoline for January rose a half cent to 72/73 cents a gallon. A December cargo of unleaded sold for 71.75 cents a gallon, brokers said.
CARB-grade gasoline saw offers rise 0.50 cent a gallon to 76 cents.
San Francisco gasoline were assessed 1.50 cents below L.A. grades, dealers said.
L.A. distillates climbed a half cent, with low sulphur diesel talked 71/72 cents and CARB-grade 73.50/74.50 cents.
After strong sales earlier this week, heavy fuel oils trailed off at $128/130 a tonne for 180 CST in Los Angeles.
"I think you'll see more business come in because the holiday's comming up," a dealer said.
